Outside rheumatology group - clinic letter
Seen 2022-03-28

Ms. Jean-Baptiste returns for routine review of her diffuse systemic sclerosis. She has had no flares that she can identify. Skin score by my exam similar to last spring; tightening limited to the hands, forearms and upper chest, no extension. No ulcers or pitting scars. No new swallowing, bowel, joint or muscle problems.
She tells me her PCP has started amlodipine and, two weeks ago, lisinopril for blood pressure. I am glad to see an ACE inhibitor on board. Clinic BP 136/86.
Medications: amlodipine 10 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, sildenafil 20 mg TID, omeprazole 20 mg daily. Allergy: nickel.
Impression: stable diffuse cutaneous SSc.
Plan: no new therapy. Keep checking BP at home; any abrupt rise, severe headache or visual change should be reported the same day. Yearly review.
Rheumatology

Follow up early next year.

events.reason: BP follow-up; spells of pounding heart and headache

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Home readings have jumped since about New Year's - many in the 150s-160s over upper 90s despite amlodipine 10, lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25, which she takes every day (pill box, pharmacy fill dates on time). For about a month she has also had spells: heart suddenly pounding, drenched in sweat, and a hard, pounding headache. They come out of nowhere, at her desk or at home, and last 10-20 minutes. Two or three a week. No chest pain, no syncope, no new meds, no decongestants, no caffeine change, no weight loss she knows of.

O: BP 158/98, recheck 156/96. HR regular. Not diaphoretic now. Thyroid not enlarged, no tremor. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: BP now uncontrolled on three agents, with paroxysmal palpitations/sweats/headache. Thinking about a secondary cause. Today BMP and TSH. Asked her to write down each spell with time and a BP reading if she can grab one. If BMP and TSH are normal and this continues, I'd like endocrine to see her. Back in 6-8 weeks, sooner if a reading is over 180/110 or a spell includes chest pain or fainting.

Plan: no change from our side. Return in one year.

orders.reason: Resistant hypertension with paroxysmal palpitations, sweating and headache

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spell diary reviewed: 14 episodes since late February. Pounding heartbeat, soaking sweat, severe headache, and on a few occasions a frightening feeling that something terrible is about to happen. She caught two readings during spells and both were well above her usual. Between spells home BP still 150s/90s. Taking all three BP meds.

BP 164/100, recheck 160/98. HR 104, regular. Looks anxious, says she is worried. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no mass. No edema.

A: Resistant hypertension with paroxysmal adrenergic-type spells. TSH and BMP normal in February. Needs a secondary hypertension evaluation.
P: Referral to endocrinology, marked urgent. Continue current meds. Reviewed ED precautions. She has the rheum and PH clinic numbers too. Will follow up once endocrine has seen her.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology - new patient consultation
Date of service: 2023-07-24
Referred by: PCP, for resistant hypertension with spells

History: 37-year-old woman with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and SSc-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension. Over roughly six months her blood pressure has become difficult to control even though she reliably takes amlodipine, lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Alongside this she has unpredictable attacks of palpitations, heavy sweating and severe headache; some come with a feeling of impending doom.
Other history: SSc (2018), PAH on sildenafil (2019), heartburn. No surgeries.
Medications: amlodipine 10 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, sildenafil 20 mg three times daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily.
Allergies: nickel (contact dermatitis).
Family history: mother - SLE. Father - essential hypertension. No relatives known to have pheochromocytoma, neurofibromatosis or an MEN syndrome.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Administrative assistant.

Exam: BP 162/98, HR 102. Anxious-appearing. Abdomen: no palpable mass, no bruit.

Results (drawn today, random, seated):
- Plasma free metanephrine 1.2 nmol/L (reference < 0.5)
- Plasma free normetanephrine 2.4 nmol/L (reference < 0.9)

Impression: Catecholamine excess well above the range expected from interfering drugs or stress, with a classic paroxysmal history. Pheochromocytoma. Her hypertension is best regarded as severe and secondary to it.

Plan:
1. Start phenoxybenzamine 10 mg twice daily. Liberal salt and fluids; expect stuffy nose and some orthostasis.
2. Once alpha blockade is established (2-3 weeks), we will add a beta blocker for heart rate. No beta blocker before then.
3. Continue amlodipine, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide and sildenafil for now.
4. Return to endocrinology in 3 months.

Thank you for this referral.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the endocrine visit. Plasma metanephrines high (1.2 and 2.4 nmol/L); endocrinology diagnosed a pheochromocytoma. Started phenoxybenzamine 10 BID on 7/24, atenolol 50 daily added 8/14. Spells down to maybe one a week and milder. Still stuffy. No fainting.

Meds reconciled: phenoxybenzamine 10 BID, atenolol 50 daily, amlodipine 10, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, sildenafil 20 TID, omeprazole 20.

BP 146/90 seated. HR slower than in April. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Pheochromocytoma - endocrinology managing; f/u there in October.
2. Hypertension - relabeled on her problem list as secondary to the pheo; essential HTN label removed. Continue all current meds.
3. BMP today with the extra drugs.
She asked good questions about what this means for her; we talked for a while. Physical in November.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology - return visit
Date of service: 2023-10-23

Interval: 37-year-old with diffuse SSc, SSc-PAH and pheochromocytoma, on phenoxybenzamine and atenolol since the summer. The adrenergic spells are much reduced. New concern: for about six months she has noticed her face getting rounder and fuller, her thighs and shoulders getting weaker (hard to climb stairs or lift files overhead), bruising with minimal bumps, more fatigue, and periods that have become irregular.
Medications: phenoxybenzamine 10 mg BID, atenolol 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, sildenafil 20 mg TID, omeprazole 20 mg daily.
Allergies: nickel (contact dermatitis).

Exam: BP 152/94. Scattered bruises on both upper arms. Proximal muscle weakness, hip flexors and deltoids 4/5.

Testing (arranged before this visit):
- Fasting glucose 112 mg/dL
- ACTH undetectable, < 5 pg/mL
- Serum cortisol 8 AM baseline 23.4 ug/dL; after high-dose overnight dexamethasone 22.9 ug/dL - no suppression

Impression: Cortisol excess that is ACTH-independent, with failure to suppress on high-dose dexamethasone. Given her catecholamine-secreting adrenal tumor, we attribute the cortisol excess to the same adrenal source.

Plan: continue phenoxybenzamine and atenolol. No new medication today. Return in 3 months. Glucose to be followed with her PCP.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
37F annual exam.

Interval history: pheochromocytoma diagnosed in July, on phenoxybenzamine + atenolol. Endocrine letter from 10/23 reviewed: facial rounding, proximal weakness, easy bruising; ACTH undetectable and cortisol did not suppress on high-dose dexamethasone; they attribute the cortisol excess to the same adrenal tumor. No new meds from them. Fasting glucose 112 there. She is tired, weaker on stairs. Spells rare now. Periods irregular since spring - some months heavier.

Meds: phenoxybenzamine 10 BID, atenolol 50, amlodipine 10, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, sildenafil 20 TID, omeprazole 20. Allergy nickel.

Exam: BP 138/86. Rounder face than last year. Bruises upper arms. Proximal strength mildly reduced. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no mass. Skin thickening hands/forearms/chest as before. No edema.

A/P
1. Pheochromocytoma with cortisol excess - endocrinology following, next visit in 3 months.
2. Secondary HTN - better than spring. Continue.
3. Glucose - CMP today; endocrine asked us to follow.
4. Irregular menses - watch; tell me if bleeding gets heavy.
5. Prevention: flu + updated COVID today. PHQ-2 1. Pap due 2024.
Labs today.
